heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Prusament PC Blend reliably within its fully enclosed build chamber, achieving a calculated safe maximum print speed of 143 mm/s at a 12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Because the stock bed caps at 100°C while PC Blend prefers 105–115°C, thermal chamber preheating and high-performance bed adhesion are strictly required.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate or Engineering Plate with PVA Glue Stick / Magigoo PC as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s under the Filament Settings > Advanced tab to automatically constrain feedrates to 143 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height.
Configure Bed Temperature to 100°C for all layers and disable the chamber exhaust fan completely (0% speed) to retain internal heat.
Reduce Part Cooling Fan to 0% for standard printing and cap Max Fan Speed at 20% only for overhangs under 25% or layers under 8 seconds.
Enable a 5mm to 8mm Brim with 0mm Brim-object gap to counteract high thermal shrinkage stress and prevent corner lifting.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Thermal contraction aggravated by the P1S bed temperature capping at 100°C, just below the optimal 105°C+ range.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the enclosed chamber by setting the bed to 100°C for 20 minutes before printing, apply liquid glue or Magigoo PC, and print with an outer brim.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or chamber drafts causing poor interlayer bonding in polycarbonate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set part cooling fan threshold to 0% min / 15% max, turn off the auxiliary cooling fan entirely, and ensure top glass and door remain closed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extrusion bubbling and rough surface finish
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption; Prusament PC Blend is hygroscopic and hydrolyzes readily at 275°C.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in an active filament dryer at 80°C for at least 8 to 12 hours prior to loading, and feed directly from a dry box.

faq.question: Can the stock Bambu P1S stainless steel nozzle handle Prusament PC Blend?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Prusament PC Blend is an unfilled polycarbonate and is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears will not suffer rapid abrasive wear.

faq.question: Is the 100°C maximum bed temperature of the P1S sufficient for PC Blend?
faq.answer: While Prusament recommends 105–115°C, 100°C is viable if you thoroughly heat-soak the P1S chamber before printing and use a quality adhesive like Magigoo PC or PVA glue stick.

faq.question: Why is an adhesive or glue stick required on a textured PEI sheet?
faq.answer: Polycarbonate bonds aggressively to PEI coatings; without a release agent like PVA glue, parts can tear chunks of PEI directly off the build plate upon removal.

faq.question: Can I print Prusament PC Blend using the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, Prusament spools fit standard AMS slots, but ensure the filament is thoroughly dried beforehand to prevent brittleness that could snap inside the PTFE paths.
